hyps.why: Removing the direct input-output path is more damaging when the node2->output path is already absent, risking disconnection.
With edge 4 absent the output relies more on the skip/direct edge, so removing it hurts more.
When the output has fewer incoming paths, adding a conv on node2->output contributes a larger share of computation.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is always zero, so a conv on node1->output does nothing.
A dead node 1 makes the node1->node2 conv ineffective.
If node 2 does not feed the output, improving node 2's input has little effect.
Without edge 4, node 1's features reach the output only indirectly or not at all, reducing the conv's value.
Replacing none restores an entire input-output path, a bigger gain than swapping an existing op.
Without the direct path, cutting node2->output can disconnect or severely starve the output node.
When node 2 is fed only by edge 1, the op on edge 1 fully determines node 2's features, amplifying the conv's benefit.
